Other Git operations were not affected. This was due to a large volume of automated, unauthenticated traffic that overwhelmed the Git LFS

timeline.label: resolved
timeline.body: On November 25, 2026, between 21:30 UTC and 00:28 UTC, Git Large File Storage (LFS) operations on github.com were degraded. During this time, an average of 2% of Git LFS requests failed, peaking at 4%. Many more requests initially failed but succeeded when Git LFS clients automatically retried them, which caused slower uploads and downloads for affected users. Other Git operations were not affected. This was due to a large volume of automated, unauthenticated traffic that overwhelmed the Git LFS servers in one of our regions, leaving them unable to respond to requests in time. timeline.body: This incident has been resolved.

timeline.body: The issue has been identified and a fix is being implemented.

timeline.label: investigating
timeline.body: Cloudflare is currently investigating issues related to Magic Transit. A subset of Magic Transit customers have a Cloudflare-managed setting enabled that clears the Don't Fragment (DF) flag. For these customers, the setting is not currently taking effect. As a result, packets with the DF flag set and larger than the tunnel MTU may be dropped. We advise customers to set an MSS clamp on their egress traffic in order to ensure ingress traffic is correctly sized.

timeline.label: resolved
timeline.body: On November 16, 2026, between 09:30 and 15:55 UTC, some pull request merges on GitHub timed out. On average, 2.9% of merge attempts timed out, with a peak of 7.1% at 15:17 UTC. Some GitHub Actions workflow runs triggered by pull requests were also delayed. Git operations such as push and fetch stayed available, with higher latency. This was a repeat of a shorter event on November 13, between 13:15 and 17:50 UTC, when 1.7% of merges timed out. Both events had the same cause: some of the storage servers that hold Git repository data reached their disk read bandwidth limits. timeline.body: On November 18, 2026, between 08:29 and 08:56 UTC, GitHub Copilot experienced degradation affecting the MAI Code 2 Flash model, causing elevated error rates for users. No other models were impacted, and users could continue using Copilot by selecting another model or Copilot Fusion. GitHub is working to further improve the resiliency of the service to prevent similar incidents in the future.

All delayed purges have since completed, and this incident has been resolved.

incidents.summary: Between November 5, 2026, at 18:02 UTC and November 19, 2026, at 18:05 UTC, GitHub users experienced unexpected expiration of their web browser sessions despite continued activity, requiring them to login. An authentication change introduced an issue that caused web requests to bypass the session activity updates and cookie renewal that normally extend session lifetime. Affected sessions consequently expired when they reached their initial expiration time. We mitigated the incident by deploying

timeline.label: resolved
timeline.body: Between November 5, 2026, at 18:02 UTC and November 19, 2026, at 18:05 UTC, GitHub users experienced unexpected expiration of their web browser sessions despite continued activity, requiring them to login. An authentication change introduced an issue that caused web requests to bypass the session activity updates and cookie renewal that normally extend session lifetime. Affected sessions consequently expired when they reached their initial expiration time. We mitigated the incident by deploying a fix to ensure that continued web activity renews session expiration and browser cookies. We are adding monitoring to detect unexpected drops in session renewal activity, helping us catch similar iss

timeline.label: monitoring
timeline.body: The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability.

timeline.label: monitoring
timeline.body: Starting around 18:02 UTC on November 5, GitHub web sessions stopped being renewed based on recent activity, so users were signed out when their sessions expired due to inactivity. These sign-outs were caused by a bug in session renewal, not due to a security incident. We believe we fixed the bug at 05:23 UTC on November 19, and sessions created since then should renew as usual. We’re continuing to monitor the situation. If you had an inactive session from that period, you may still find that you’re signed out when you return to GitHub. If that happens, all you need to do is sign back in.
